title: Openness of the ambient regular locus along a J-2 closed fibre
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $I\subseteq A$ be an ideal, and let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a finite-type morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-affine-spectrum] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Assume $A/I$ is J-2: for every finite-type $A/I$-algebra, the set of primes whose local rings are regular local is open [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Put $Z=f^{-1}V(I)$, with its subspace topology. Then $\{x\in Z:\mathcal O_{X,x}\text{ is regular local}\}$ is open in $Z$ [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Equivalently, $W=\{x\in Z:\mathcal O_{X,x}\text{ is not regular local}\}$ is closed in $X$. This uses the local rings of $X$, not the local rings of the closed subscheme defined by $I\mathcal O_X$.

source.place: Kurano–Shimomoto, Lemma 4.2 and Claim 4.3, printed pp.4–5. No Stacks tag states this relative ambient-regular-locus assertion. The J-2 hypothesis has its definition in Stacks More on Algebra, definition-J. Archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Work on a finite affine cover $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $X$ with $B$ a finite-type $A$-algebra, supplied by the finite-type hypothesis. The finite-type Noetherian algebra lemma makes both $B$ and $C=B/IB$ Noetherian (the latter is also finite type over $A$). The quotient-spectrum homeomorphism identifies $Z\cap U=V(IB)$ with $\operatorname{Spec}C$. The affine stalk isomorphism identifies $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ with $B_{\mathfrak p_x}$. Thus on this chart we must show that $E=\{\mathfrak p\in V(IB):B_{\mathfrak p}\text{ is regular local}\}$ is open in $V(IB)$.

source.place: Lemma 4.2, first sentence of proof (affine reduction); Stacks 00FN lemma-Noetherian-permanence, 00E5 lemma-spec-closed, 01HV lemma-spec-sheaves.

proof.text: If $\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak q$ and $B_{\mathfrak q}$ is regular local, the prime correspondence supplies $Q=\mathfrak pB_{\mathfrak q}$, and $(B_{\mathfrak q})_Q\cong B_{\mathfrak p}$ by the localization-of-localization isomorphism. Regular local rings remain regular local at primes. Hence regularity is stable under generalization in $\operatorname{Spec}B$, and in particular within $V(IB)$.

source.place: Lemma 4.2, final paragraph, generalization stability; Stacks 00E3 lemma-spec-localization and 0AFS lemma-localization-of-regular-local-is-regular.

proof.text: Every nonempty irreducible closed subset of $V(IB)$ is $V(\mathfrak q)$ for a prime $\mathfrak q\supseteq IB$, using the quotient-spectrum homeomorphism and the classification of irreducible closed subsets of a spectrum. If $B_{\mathfrak q}$ is not regular local, no $B_{\mathfrak p}$ with $\mathfrak p\supseteq\mathfrak q$ can be regular, by step 2. Then $V(\mathfrak q)$ itself is a nonempty relatively open subset disjoint from $E$. It remains to produce a nonempty open subset contained in $E$ when $B_{\mathfrak q}$ is regular local.

source.place: Claim 4.3, reduction to Z=V(q) and the case q not in Reg(X); Stacks 00ES lemma-irreducible.

proof.text: Assume $B_{\mathfrak q}$ is regular local. Since $\mathfrak q\supseteq IB$, the quotient $B/\mathfrak q$ is finite type over $A/I$: the images of any finite set of algebra generators of $B$ still generate it, and $I$ acts by zero. The J-2 assumption therefore makes its regular locus open. This locus contains its generic point, since $B/\mathfrak q$ is a domain and its localization at zero is its fraction field, a regular local ring of dimension zero and maximal ideal zero. By the basic-open basis choose $b\notin\mathfrak q$ such that $(B/\mathfrak q)_{\mathfrak p/\mathfrak q}$ is regular local whenever $\mathfrak p\supseteq\mathfrak q$ and $b\notin\mathfrak p$.

source.place: Claim 4.3, equation (4.1); Stacks 07P7 definition-J and 00E0 lemma-Zariski-topology.

proof.text: Choose $d=\dim B_{\mathfrak q}$ generators of its maximal ideal. Write each as $a_i/s_i$ with $a_i\in\mathfrak q$, $s_i\notin\mathfrak q$. Replacing each generator by its unit multiple $a_i/1$ preserves the generated ideal. The resulting system of parameters is a regular sequence by the regular-local generators lemma. The principal-neighbourhood lemma supplies $g\notin\mathfrak q$ such that $a_1,\ldots,a_d$ is a regular sequence in $B_g$. This includes $d=0$, when the sequence is empty.

source.place: Claim 4.3, maximal ideal generated by a regular sequence; Stacks 00NQ lemma-regular-ring-CM and 061L lemma-regular-sequence-in-neighbourhood.

proof.text:
Let $K=(a_1,\ldots,a_d)\subseteq\mathfrak q$. Noetherianity gives finitely many generators $t_j$ of $\mathfrak q$. Since $KB_{\mathfrak q}=\mathfrak qB_{\mathfrak q}$, ideal-membership clearing supplies $s_j
otin\mathfrak q$ with $s_jt_j\in K$. Put $s=\prod_j s_j
otin\mathfrak q$. Then $s\mathfrak q\subseteq K$, because $st_j=(\prod_{l
e j}s_l)(s_jt_j)\in K$ and the $t_j$ generate $\mathfrak q$. For every prime $\mathfrak p$ avoiding $s$, the element $s/1$ is invertible in $B_{\mathfrak p}$, whence $KB_{\mathfrak p}=\mathfrak qB_{\mathfrak p}$. Empty generating sets use the product $1$.

source.place: Claim 4.3, shrinking so that q is generated by the chosen regular sequence; Stacks 07P9 lemma-intersection-regular-with-closed, the same denominator-clearing step.

proof.text: Put $h=bgs\notin\mathfrak q$. For $\mathfrak p\supseteq\mathfrak q$ avoiding $h$, localize $B_g$ further at the prime corresponding to $\mathfrak p$; this ring is $B_{\mathfrak p}$, with $a_i/1$ unchanged (both invert exactly the elements required by the fraction localization). Weak regularity survives this localization. Since all $a_i\in\mathfrak p$, their final quotient is nonzero, so they are a regular sequence in $B_{\mathfrak p}$. Step 6 identifies their ideal with $\mathfrak qB_{\mathfrak p}$. The quotient-localization isomorphism gives $B_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak qB_{\mathfrak p}\cong(B/\mathfrak q)_{\mathfrak p/\mathfrak q}$, regular by step 4. The ring $B_{\mathfrak p}$ is Noetherian and local; lifting regularity from this regular-sequence quotient proves it regular. Thus $V(\mathfrak q)\cap D(h)$ is a nonempty relatively open subset contained in $E$.

source.place: Claim 4.3, the assertion that all primes in V(q) outside V(q+fB) are regular; Stacks 00CT proposition-localize-quotient, 00FN lemma-Noetherian-permanence and 00NU lemma-regular-mod-x.

proof.text: Apply the Noetherian constructibility criterion to $Y=\operatorname{Spec}C$ and the subset corresponding to $E$. It applies since $C$ is Noetherian, so $Y$ has a one-element affine Noetherian cover. For every irreducible closed subset the nonempty open subset required by that criterion was constructed in steps 3 and 7. Thus $E$ is constructible in $\operatorname{Spec}C$. Step 2 gives generalization stability in this spectrum, because prime inclusion in $C$ corresponds to prime inclusion in $B$ among primes containing $IB$. The constructible-generalization-open lemma for spectra makes $E$ open in $\operatorname{Spec}C$, hence open in $Z\cap U$.

source.place: Claim 4.3 and Lemma 4.2, final paragraph; Stacks 053Z lemma-characterize-constructible-Noetherian and 00I0 lemma-constructible-stable-specialization-closed (2).

proof.text: The sets $Z\cap U$ are open in $Z$ and cover it, so the union of their relatively open regular loci is open in $Z$. The complement $W$ is closed in $Z$. Finally $V(I)$ is closed in $\operatorname{Spec}A$ and the underlying map of a scheme morphism is continuous, so $Z=f^{-1}V(I)$ is closed in $X$. A subset closed in a closed subspace is closed in the ambient space: writing $W=Z\cap F$ for a closed $F\subseteq X$ proves the asserted closedness of $W$ in $X$. Conversely that closedness gives openness of $Z\setminus W$ in $Z$.

source.place: Lemma 4.2, affine-to-global passage; equivalence with ambient closedness used immediately in Lemma 4.4, printed p.5.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q93-e6e41db2e (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and all 24 cited statements in full. The statement is unchanged against the live clone. The 9-step proof, which adds no new nodes, is the J-2 relativisation of Stacks More on Algebra 07P9 (lemma-intersection-regular-with-closed), read at more-algebra.tex lines 11611-11640. Kurano-Shimomoto is not in literature/, so the report lists it as WANTED and proof_origin.by is agent. The step-by-step checks: step 1 uses 00FN, 00E5 and the affine stalk localization; step 2 uses 00E3 and 0AFS for generalization; step 3 uses 00ES and shows a non-regular V(q) is disjoint from E. In step 4, J-2 of A/I is applied to B/q (finite type over A/I), and the regular generic point plus 00E0 give b not in q. In step 5, 00NQ and 061L are applied to the a_i in the Noetherian ring B. Step 6 clears denominators explicitly, giving s.q contained in K. In step 7, weak regularity localizes, the final quotient is nonzero because the a_i lie in p, 00CT gives the quotient, and 00NU lifts regularity. The identification of B_p with the localization of B_g at pB_g is a two-line fact written in the step; I accept it under the C1 short-fact exception. Step 8 uses 053Z on Spec C, then generalization stability and 00I0(2). Step 9 is elementary closedness. Small cases checked: I=A, I=0, d=0, and B=k[eps]/(eps^2), where W=X. There is no cycle. The five declared tool_uses are generic commutative algebra and topology, and I accept them. Batch 5: the three flagged citations are generic and outside both assumptions. lem-exc-regular-local-lift-regular-sequence-quotient is Stacks 00NU, and its closure reaches only the Mathlib leaf lem-trf-regular-sequence-dimension-formula. lem-trf-noetherian-constructible-subset-criterion is Stacks 053Z, Noetherian topology. lem-trf-spectrum-constructible-generalization-open is Stacks 00I0, a Mathlib leaf. None is a step of the trace formula or of Poincare duality. I made no changes.

lean.statement: theorem isOpen_regularLocus_on_j2_closedFibre (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A) (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of A)) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] (hJ : ∀ (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra (A ⧸ I) B] [Algebra.FiniteType (A ⧸ I) B], IsOpen {p : PrimeSpectrum B | IsRegularLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)}) : IsOpen {x : {x : X // f x ∈ PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set A)} | IsRegularLocalRing (X.presheaf.stalk x.1)} ∧ IsClosed {x : X | f x ∈ PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set A) ∧ ¬ IsRegularLocalRing (X.presheaf.stalk x)}

reviewed_lean.note: Clause-by-clause match. Noetherian A, arbitrary I, finite type = LocallyOfFiniteType+QuasiCompact (matches the record). hJ is the J-2 part of the recorded IsQuasiExcellent at A⧸I, verbatim, universe u, no Noetherian/G-ring added. Both conclusions use ambient X.presheaf.stalk: open in the subtype f⁻¹V(I) and W closed in X, the node's two equivalent forms. IsRegularLocalRing is the recorded ring notion. Only the lean field changed versus live; statement verbatim in file; proof is sorry only; docstrings have the source place, blueprint tag and nine proof steps; no new defs. Edge cases I=A, I=0, empty X, k[ε]/ε² checked. Note only: upstream IsJ2 is definitionally the same as hJ. No compile run since no change; worker's compile is clean.
